PullRequest.Title: automations: fix: honor worktree and provider session configuration
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

An automation stores two different kinds of state. Its target identifies the provider, agent/session type, workspace, isolation mode, and base branch. Its provider-owned session template stores model selection and model options, a custom agent, and native configuration such as Mode and Approvals.

Both must survive editing and later execution. The browser can dispatch a legacy automation, while a migrated automation runs directly in the Agent Host, including after a host restart. Saved preferences are not permission grants: the current provider schema and managed policy still determine effective behavior.

## What was broken

The Automation dialog gated New Worktree on a Copilot-CLI-only declaration, even though worktree isolation is implemented by the shared host for other agents, including Claude and Codex. It also asked the local Git extension for every target's repository. That extension rejects remote workspace URIs, so merely enabling the checkbox would not fix remote automations.

Several adjacent configuration paths were also incomplete:

- Generic provider configuration lived in the ordinary composer's repository toolbar, which the Automation dialog did not render.
- Cloud model restoration updated the displayed model but bypassed the extension's model option. A late option catalogue could therefore disagree with the displayed selection.
- Cloud Sandbox routing came from an unrelated ordinary-composer preference rather than the saved automation.
- Restored fallback-CLI approval preferences overwrote the initially policy-clamped value.
- A host automation inherited its creation-time model into the first message, but not its selected custom agent.
- Host-generated session IDs were marked worktree-pending too late to prevent Codex prewarming in the source checkout.
- Codex workspace-agent URI matching did not account for worktree execution, especially when subsequent or restored turns repeated the original agent selection.

## How the fixes work

### Provider-owned worktree discovery

`ISessionsProvider.getWorktreeOptions` now exposes workspace-specific worktree support, the current branch, initial branch choices, and an optional loader for incomplete result sets.

Agent Host providers resolve these choices on the selected host. Branch searches reuse that resolved configuration rather than re-resolving the full schema for every query. Providers without the operation retain the existing local Git path.

This keeps shared Automation UI provider-neutral. The static Agent Host declaration no longer singles out Copilot; the host's workspace schema determines whether worktrees can actually be chosen.

Remote completion windows are not treated as complete branch inventories. A saved or searched branch outside the initial window is not falsely marked unavailable. Search immediately removes selectable stale results, exposes loading, and supports retry. Related target/provider notifications are coalesced before starting repository work. Shared IME cancellation behavior is explicitly outside this PR's scope.

If a saved Worktree target becomes unsupported, its checkbox can still be unchecked. After opting out, normal repository availability checks must pass before Worktree can be enabled again. Explicit worktree targets submitted through the automation tool also resolve workspace-specific support before persistence.

### Provider-native session controls and preferences

The Automation controls reuse native provider configuration pickers. Generic enum/boolean settings are available alongside dedicated provider Mode and Approvals controls, without duplicating worktree/branch controls or exposing transient/session-only fields.

Cloud automations can display and save the existing Sandbox choice. Restoration does not rewrite ordinary-composer defaults. Explicit picker changes retain the existing shared-default semantics.

Cloud model selection now synchronizes its extension option through the same path for interactive changes, template restoration, and late option discovery. Canonical values take precedence over compatibility aliases, and unknown provider preferences remain intact.

Fallback CLI approvals retain the saved preference separately from the policy-effective observable value. Display and execution use the effective value; capture preserves unchanged intent.

### Execution and custom agents

The first host automation message inherits creation-time model and agent selections independently, while preserving explicit message overrides.

Session IDs are allocated before provider creation, so both supplied and generated IDs are worktree-pending before eager provider work can start. Failure paths clear the pending state.

Codex resolves original workspace-agent selections at customization launch using host worktree metadata and canonical repository roots. It preserves the original persisted selection rather than rewriting protocol identity. Regression coverage includes repeated `changeAgent` calls, provider reload, linked source checkouts, and plugin/external selections that must not be redirected.

## Provider coverage and intentional limits

| Provider | Worktree behavior | Configuration coverage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local/remote Agent Host Copilot CLI | Host schema and host branch discovery | Model/options, custom agent, native Mode/Approvals, opaque template values |
| Local/remote Agent Host Claude | Same host-owned isolation path | Model/options, custom agent, native permission-mode configuration |
| Local/remote Agent Host Codex | Same path, with pending-start and agent-restoration repairs | Model/options, custom agent, native mode/approval presets |
| Other schema-driven Agent Hosts | Capability comes from the workspace schema, not the provider name | Generic supported controls remain provider-owned |
| Fallback Copilot CLI | Existing local Git/worktree path | Model/options, custom modes/agents, saved versus effective approvals |
| Copilot Cloud | Worktrees remain unsupported | Cloud model option and saved Sandbox routing |

Cloud custom agents and workspace-less Cloud sessions remain unsupported. Transient local Dev Container handoff controls are not newly made into Automation template fields; selecting an existing remote/container host continues through the remote-provider boundary. No new protocol fields, user settings, dependencies, or policy channels are introduced.

## Shared ActionList scope

This PR makes **no changes** to `src/vs/platform/actionWidget/browser/actionList.ts` or its tests. The two shared IME fixes have been removed from this branch and are delivered separately in [#335578](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335578).

This deliberately allows the provider/worktree fixes to land without changing a component consumed by many unrelated surfaces. Until the separate IME fix lands, cancelling IME composition during a pending remote branch search while retaining the same query can leave that picker loading. Changing the query or reopening the picker remains the workaround. That edge case is not claimed fixed by this PR.

## Resolved follow-up fixes

The two worktree follow-up fixes remain in this PR. The shared IME follow-up has moved to separate delivery:

1. **Workspace validation in the tool** ([ad39403b982](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/ad39403b982)): explicit worktree targets use the selected provider's `getWorktreeOptions` before creation or update. Missing repositories and unsupported results become tool input errors. Registered legacy providers without the optional operation keep their previous behavior. Cancellation interrupts a pending lookup without writing; provider errors propagate rather than becoming successful targets. Non-worktree and unrelated partial updates do not perform repository discovery.
2. **Unavailable Worktree recovery** ([1729876db3a](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/1729876db3a)): the saved-branch exception applies only while Worktree is active. Users can still opt out, but cannot turn Worktree back on while repository discovery is missing, loading, failed, or empty.
3. **Narrow shared IME retries:** removed from this PR together with the initial shared IME fix, for independent component-level review and landing.

All four Astra lenses reviewed the complete six-file follow-up diff and returned **Ship**, with no findings or file modifications.

## Rebase on current main

The original fixes were subsequently rebased onto `5559183ea8eeb0fda5cdce67967f9bdc3af6e2e5`. Resolutions preserve upstream combobox/type-to-filter tests, Codex workspace-less customization filtering and telemetry, relocated Dev Container controls, and updated provider imports. The reload regression now answers the upstream thread metadata read before resume. Test adaptations remain folded into the owning fixes.

The later extraction removed exactly the two ActionList commits: both shared files match the base, and every other file is byte-for-byte identical to the pre-extraction branch. Both handled Copilot review threads remain resolved.

## Validation

After removing the shared ActionList changes:

- **308 targeted tests passed** across automation tools/dialog/model, upstream ActionWidget suites, and existing dynamic-picker consumers.
- Confirmed that both ActionList files have zero diff against the PR base.
- Confirmed that every other file is unchanged from the previously tested branch.
- The remaining history contains **15 focused fix commits**.

Rebase validation:

- **1,408 affected unit tests passed**, with 27 existing pending tests.
- After the final upstream Codex image-attachment update, **103 focused Codex tests passed**, including worktree/prewarm coverage. These overlap the earlier selection and are not an additional unique-test total.
- **Five strict real-provider replay scenarios passed again** on the final rebased tree.
- TypeScript, layering, changed-file lint, diff checks, and normal commit hygiene passed with dependencies restored from the current main lockfile.

Follow-up validation:

- **232 targeted tests passed** across the automation tool/dialog/isolation model, shared ActionWidget suites, and both existing Agent Host dynamic-picker consumers.
- Regression-first testing reproduced the four invalid re-enablement states and both completed-search retry states before their fixes.
- `npm run typecheck-client`, six-file ESLint, `git diff --check`, and each commit's normal hygiene hook passed.

Earlier validation of the original implementation:

- **1,195 unit tests passed**, with **27 existing pending tests**, across the affected Automation, provider, Codex, and shared ActionWidget suites.
- **Five strict replay E2E scenarios passed** using the real bundled runtimes and AHP:
  - Host session configuration resolves and completes Git branches.
  - Correct working-directory creation for Copilot CLI, Claude, and Codex.
  - Copilot automation Mode and Approvals survive a host restart and run.
- `npm run typecheck-client` passed.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` passed.
- Changed-file ESLint and `git diff --check` passed.

The replay scenarios use committed model traffic, not live model services. Cloud and arbitrary remote deployment behavior is covered at the provider-adapter boundary; no paid Cloud runs or live third-party remote-host jobs were launched.

## Review

Two complete independent four-lens Astra reviews covered architecture, performance, UI/UX, and correctness/simplicity. All findings were addressed with regressions. Astra then independently verified the final IME-cancellation and duplicate-lookup follow-ups and reported no remaining evidence-backed issues in those repairs.

Later Copilot review identified two worktree validation issues, and a shared-component scope review identified the completed-request retry concern. A complete four-lens Astra review of the follow-up fixes returned Ship in every lens. The two worktree fixes remain here; the reviewed shared-component fixes have since been deliberately extracted for independent landing.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new tool call path is explicit: ConfigureAutomationTool awaits getWorktreeOptions for every newly supplied worktree target and reads only supportsWorktree, while the Agent Host implementation always invokes loadBranches with an empty query. That completion runs three Git operations and getBranches executes an uncapped for-each-ref before the 25-item result limit is applied. The exact duration varies by repository and remote-host latency, but the extra critical-path work and its scaling are established.
Findings.PerformanceResource: A remote Agent Host IPC plus Git subprocesses, including uncapped refs output and parsing
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One eager completion per explicit worktree create/update; subprocess output and parsing grow with the repository's number of local branches, regardless of the 25-item post-processing limit.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased configure-automation tool latency and unnecessary Git CPU/I/O before persistence
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, ConfigureAutomationTool validated the static session-type capability and proceeded without provider IPC or Git branch enumeration.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every explicit worktree target now calls getWorktreeOptions; Agent Host providers resolve the schema and then eagerly request empty-query branch completions even for the capability-only tool caller.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line `? await loadBranches('', token)` eagerly invokes the dynamic branch loader. The new ConfigureAutomationTool path awaits `provider.getWorktreeOptions(...)` for a worktree target but subsequently inspects only `options?.supportsWorktree`.
Findings.Title: Avoid enumerating every branch for capability-only validation
Findings.Impact: Creating or updating a worktree automation through the tool is blocked on avoidable remote IPC and `git for-each-ref`/current/default-branch subprocess work. Repositories with large branch sets pay growing output/parsing cost although validation only needs workspace support.
Findings.Evidence: `ConfigureAutomationTool.resolveAvailableTarget` awaits `provider.getWorktreeOptions` and only checks `options?.supportsWorktree`. In this implementation, dynamic schemas always execute `loadBranches('')`; `AgentService.sessionConfigCompletions` routes this to `WorktreeIsolation.branchCompletions`, which runs getBranches, getCurrentBranch, and getDefaultBranch. `AgentHostGitService.getBranches` uses `git for-each-ref` without a count, and the 25-item completion limit is applied only afterward.
Findings.Recommendation: Provide a capability-only path (or an option that skips branch loading) for tool validation, and perform `loadBranches` only in the branch-picker scenario that consumes the results.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: For host-generated worktree session IDs, the old code could not mark isolation pending before Codex createChat scheduled an eager prewarm. Codex then materialized a thread in the source checkout; first send had to await that stale materialization, unsubscribe it, and materialize again in the new worktree.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Worktree-backed Codex sessions with host-generated IDs performed a wasted prewarm and could delay the first turn while the stale thread was cleaned up and recreated.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The host now mints the session URI before provider creation and marks that exact ID pending, so Codex's prewarm guard sees it and skips eager materialization until the worktree working directory is finalized.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The changed `_createProviderSession` now computes `session` and calls `notePending` before `provider.chats.createChat`. Codex `_createChat` calls `_schedulePrewarm`, whose pending check suppresses `_materializeIfNeeded`; without it, `_adoptWorkingDirectoryBeforeSend` awaits and unsubscribes the stale prewarm before changing cwd. The expanded test proves both client- and host-generated IDs are pending during provider creation. Blame attributes the old conditional pending-ID logic to the supplied introducing commit.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Automation dialog, switch workspace/provider/session type, and search worktree branches
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The dialog schedules and coalesces repository reloads, then waits for provider-owned worktree options before enabling branch selection. For Agent Host providers, schema resolution completes before the initial branch completion; typed searches wait for a 200 ms delayer and then a completion response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: resolveSessionConfig on the selected local or remote Agent Host
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The dialog asked the local Git extension to open the selected repository; remote workspace URIs could not be resolved there.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks initial worktree capability and branch-picker readiness

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Git repository/root, HEAD, current/default branch, and local-ref discovery on the selected host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Initial resolution performs repository/HEAD/current/default checks, followed by one initial branch completion; each effective search performs branch/current/default reads
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Local targets used local Git-extension repository/ref discovery; remote targets did not have working provider-owned discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the initial picker and each remote branch-search result

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One initial lookup per coalesced folder/target/session-type state, plus one effective completion for the latest debounced query. Git ref production scans the repository's local branches; returned suggestions are capped to 25 only after the scan.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Folder, target, and session-type notifications share a zero-delay RunOnceScheduler and cancel the superseded request. Initial schema resolution and initial completion are sequential. Search requests are delayed/coalesced and use cancellation tokens rather than fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: AgentHostGitService caches successful repository-root and primary-worktree mappings in bounded LRU caches, but current/default branch and refs are re-read. No branch-result cache is introduced; canceled/stale UI responses are discarded.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the UI-to-provider-to-Agent-Host and Git call chain is explicit in the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote-host round-trip and repository branch counts vary, but notification coalescing and search cancellation bound request concurrency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding for the dialog itself: provider-owned discovery is required for remote correctness, initial requests are coalesced, searches are debounced/canceled, and there is no multiplicative fan-out beyond the selected target.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or update an automation with an explicit worktree target through ConfigureAutomationTool
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before the automation write can proceed, resolveAvailableTarget awaits provider.getWorktreeOptions and checks only supportsWorktree.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provider getWorktreeOptions, including Agent Host schema resolution and dynamic branch completion
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider lookup containing two sequential Agent Host requests per explicit worktree mutation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the in-memory advertised session-type capability was checked; no provider/host boundary was crossed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks create/update even though the caller consumes only supportsWorktree

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Git capability probes followed by getBranches/current/default branch commands; getBranches executes uncapped git for-each-ref
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Capability probes plus three completion operations per worktree validation; refs output scales with branch count
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Git subprocess was started by tool target validation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All operations complete before automation persistence

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One validation per create/update that supplies a worktree target. The unnecessary Git ref output and parsing scale with all local branches in the selected repository.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Validation is serialized before persistence; resolveSessionConfig is followed by initial branch completion, so the work cannot overlap the write or be skipped on a valid target.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Repository-root discovery may hit a bounded cache, but refs/current/default branch reads are not cached. There is no capability-only cache or call mode.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the caller reads only supportsWorktree while getWorktreeOptions unconditionally awaits loadBranches with an empty query.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Absolute delay depends on host latency and repository branch count; the extra subprocess/IPC sequence is unconditional for dynamic Agent Host branch schemas.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager-work regression: capability-only validation newly blocks on branch enumeration that it never consumes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create and first-send a Codex worktree session when the host generates the session ID
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session config is resolved, the host now mints and marks the session ID pending before provider createChat, and Codex's prewarm check returns without materializing. The actual worktree and Codex thread are created on first send.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Codex thread prewarm/materialization and later stale-thread unsubscribe/rematerialization
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously up to one wasted prewarm and replacement per host-ID worktree session; now zero before worktree finalization
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Client-supplied IDs were marked pending, but host-generated IDs were unavailable to the pending check until after provider creation, allowing eager Codex materialization in the source checkout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The stale prewarm could be awaited and unsubscribed on the first-send path; the changed pending marker removes it

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One session creation and one first-send transition; without the fix, each affected session could create one stale prewarmed thread and then replace it.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Host side-effect initialization and provider creation run in parallel. Pending state is established before that concurrency begins. First-send worktree resolution remains serialized per session.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The pending marker is in-memory session state and is cleared on non-provisional creation or rollback. Codex SDK availability is separately cached; no new retained cache is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high; the Codex createChat/prewarm and first-send cleanup path is directly traced and regression-tested for both ID sources.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The saved time depends on SDK/process readiness and prewarm completion timing, but the eliminated duplicate materialization path is explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: This PR fixes a real eager-work regression; it was recorded through report_regression_fix and is not a review finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send or restore Codex turns with a selected workspace agent in a host-owned worktree
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each customization launch resolves the selected agent in parallel with existing workspace-agent and skill discovery, then reads the selected agent file before thread start/resume/turn dispatch. A first turn can build customization more than once; later sends rebuild to detect workspace changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the session database and read four worktree metadata keys
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Customization builds used the persisted source agent URI directly and did not read worktree metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in parallel with existing customization discovery but must finish before launch signature and thread request construction

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check worktree-path existence and read the resolved worktree agent file
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A constant number per applicable build; selected-agent file reading already existed but now targets the worktree copy
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No worktree metadata stat was required; the selected source agent file was read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before thread start/resume or turn dispatch

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve repository and primary worktree roots for linked source checkouts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold linked-source resolution can run repository-root/worktree-list Git probes; successful mappings are reused afterward
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No repository-identity validation was performed for selected agents.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One metadata resolution per customization build for the narrow case where the selected URI is under sourceRoot/.github/agents and differs from the runtime working directory; first sends/restores may invoke the build twice, later sends generally once.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Metadata resolution runs in Promise.all with existing discovery. Customization reconciliation is sequenced per session. Successful repository-root and primary-worktree probes are cached.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Worktree metadata database reads and the worktree-path existence check are repeated; repository-root and primary-worktree mappings use bounded caches. Re-reading the agent file is intentional so edits are detected between turns.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added operations and frequency; lower for a meaningful independent user-visible regression because the work is constant, parallelized, cached where expensive, and required to preserve edited worktree instructions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Database backend and filesystem latency vary, and this path is limited to selected native workspace agents in worktrees. Existing customization discovery already performs filesystem work on the same path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the added identity checks are narrowly gated and cold Git probes are cached; evidence does not establish a material performance regression beyond small constant work on an already asynchronous customization path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore or change Copilot Cloud model/sandbox configuration and render provider-native automation controls
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Model restoration synchronizes the matching option when available; a late option catalog performs one synchronization before notifying UI listeners. Sandbox and generic controls read local observable/configuration state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize the chosen cloud model into the contributed session option state
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one set operation per explicit model selection or relevant option-catalog arrival for the active transient session
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Interactive model changes explicitly set the option, while restoration and late catalogs could leave it unset.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local session-option update precedes send so the extension can honor the model; no collection fan-out was found

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One transient new-session object and one selected model item; option lookup scales with the small model option group. Option-catalog events are infrequent.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Updates are synchronous local state operations; model/source observables are committed in one transaction. No loop is formed because session-option changes do not fire option-group catalog changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Selected options are held only for the transient session and disposed or transferred when the placeholder commits. Sandbox preference uses profile storage.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the call path and bounded cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The underlying extension-host implementation can vary, but the changed cardinality is constant and short-lived.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: synchronization is constant-sized, scoped to a transient session, and necessary before send; no repeated event loop or unbounded retention is introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 22 changed files and traced the changed UI, tool, Agent Host, Git, Codex, and cloud-option paths. Reported one medium eager-work regression: capability-only automation validation unnecessarily enumerates branches. Also recorded the host-generated Codex worktree pending-ID change as a verified regression fix.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
